author: cskiraly
content:
Are you about this <@792404665068158998> ?
The BAL can be generated during ececution of the payload. It is a sideproduct of execution others CAN use to speed-up execution.
I was always under the impression you can execute, get the BAL, hash it, and validate that hash.

author: m.kalinin
content: `engine_notifyBlockAccessListV1` would fit nicely if BAL is optional for the execution, in the most of the cases this call would be made before `newPayload` but if not then the payload is executed without BAL

author: nero_eth
content: Right that's what you do and in the end you compare that the BAL hash generated during execution matches the bal hash put in the block header.

author: nero_eth
content:
So, there are 2 BALs, at least in the specs: the one that comes from the CL, is hashed and only the hash enters the stf. And the one that is generated during execution, then hashed to be compared to tha bal hash in the header.
This guarantees that what you used for parallelizing is 100% correct.

author: cskiraly
content:
In other words, BAL accounting and BAL verification are data structure consistency requirements. Where we hash, what we deliver in what order are performance and thus timing related.
I'm saying this bacause from what you wroite in the beginning felt like BAL is now a pre-condition to execute. It is not, state and transaction list is still enough to verify the consistency of the data structure, it might just be too slow under a few conditions. The conditions that should hold for BAL to be the required for timely execution are:
- high gas block,
- low (minimum according to spec) power machine
- highly dependent execution chain in the data.
If one these are not there, you can execute without a BAL with speculative parallelization, record the BAL while doing it, verify consistency, and call it a day.

author: nero_eth

author: nero_eth

author: m.kalinin
content: and have a separate optional call for warming up that will be used in a happy case

author: nero_eth
content: It's not a precondition for executing but many clients validate the BAL while executing - and starting to execute without the BAL is possible but introduces a lot of complexity. E.g. would you then still use the classical prefetcher, or what do you do when the BAL arrives, parallelize from there on, and validate what you already executed against the BAL. Things turn unclean quickly and the simple and clean solution would be to just never begin execution without the BAL (if clients want to they can optimize for that but they won't gain anything as we wouldn't scale such that this optimization is ever needed - esp since in the worst-case the BAL arrives before the payload, having an ealier deadline)

author: nero_eth
content: I see so have `engine_notifyBlockAccessListV1` and in addition just keep newPayload as is, cache the early bal on the CL and then pass it to the EL together with the payload

author: m.kalinin
content: yeah, I think it's fine too. I would move BAL outside of ExecutionPayload into a separate `newPayload` param as with this EIP it becomes a sidecar and I guess isn't a part of ExecutionPayload structure on the CL side anymore
